ToolExecutionCompleteResult(content='1. # Structure and semantics
2. 
3. Regions/landmarks, heading outline, and view title.
4. 
5. ## Web implementation
6. 
7. ### Landmarks
8. 
9. - Use `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>` for their semantic roles. Avoid `role="banner"`, `role="navigation"`, `role="main"`, `role="contentinfo"` on generic elements unless a native landmark can't be used.
10. - Exactly one `<main>` per page. On multi-page sites, make `<main id="maincontent" tabindex="-1">` the bypass-block target.
11. - If multiple landmarks of the same kind exist (e.g., two `<nav>`), give each a unique accessible name via `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
12. - Complementary content uses `<aside>`. Search regions use `role="search"` on a `<form>` or a wrapping element.
13. 
14. ### Heading outline
15. 
16. - One `<h1>` per page, typically the first heading inside `<main>` describing the page topic.
17. - Do not skip levels (no `<h1>` → `<h3>`). Nest sections by level.
18. - Headings label sections of content, not decorative breaks. Do not use heading tags purely for styling.
19. - Visually hidden headings may label regions for AT; keep them short and descriptive.
20. 
21. ### Page title
22. 
23. - Every document has a descriptive `<title>`. Prefer `Unique page — section — site` (most specific first).

Cat FAQ

Understanding the mysterious world of cats, one purr at a time.

Cats purr for many reasons, not just when they're happy. While it is often a sign of contentment, cats also purr to self-soothe, heal their bodies, and even communicate with their kittens. The frequency of a cat's purr has been shown to improve bone density and promote healing.

Cats are crepuscular, meaning they are most active during dawn and dusk. They sleep an average of 12 to 16 hours a day to conserve energy for hunting. In the wild, hunting requires intense bursts of energy, so their long naps ensure they are ready for the next "pounce."

Boxes provide cats with a sense of security and safety. In a confined space, they feel protected from predators and can observe their surroundings without being seen. Boxes also help cats stay warm, as the cardboard acts as an insulator.

Whiskers are highly sensitive tactile hairs that act as a cat's radar. They help cats navigate in the dark, detect changes in air currents, and determine if they can fit through tight spaces. Never trim a cat's whiskers, as it can make them feel disoriented and confused.

Kneading, or "making biscuits," is a behavior cats carry over from kittenhood. Kittens knead their mothers to stimulate milk flow. In adulthood, it's a sign of extreme comfort and happiness, often performed on soft surfaces or their favorite humans.
